match.reason: No bank point teaches checking the same indicators after a change to judge whether the strategy worked; the closest, Measuring performance, only covers types of indicators and comparing them over time at a Units 1 and 2 accounting level, and the staff performance management card is about appraising workers, not evaluating change.

draft.title: Reviewing performance indicators after change
card: A performance indicator is a measure of how a business is doing, such as sales, costs, staff turnover or customer complaints.
Before a change, managers record the indicators they hope the change will improve. This gives them a starting point to compare against.

After the change, managers measure the same indicators again and compare the results with the starting point. If the numbers have moved the way the managers wanted, the strategy is likely to have worked.
If the numbers have not moved as hoped, managers can adjust the change or try a different strategy. Other events, such as a rival's price cut, can also affect results.
draft.remember: Measure the same indicators before and after, then compare to judge the change.

a.q: Why do managers measure the same indicators after a change that they measured before it?
opts: To compare the results and judge whether the change worked
To show staff that the change has now been completed
To choose which indicators to use for the next change
To prove that the original strategy was the right choice
a.why: Using the same indicators lets managers compare the new results with the starting point. Proving the strategy right is tempting, but a review may show it did not work, and managers then adjust it.
a.clue: Think about what a fair comparison needs.

b.q: Hana owns a bakery in Geelong. She introduces online ordering to reduce customer complaints about long queues. Before the change there were 40 complaints a month. Which review is the best way to judge the change?
opts: Count complaints after a month and compare them with 40
Count online orders after the change and compare with sales
Ask staff whether they like the new online ordering system
Check that the online ordering system has been installed
b.why: The aim was to cut complaints, and the starting point was 40 a month. Counting complaints again gives a fair comparison. Counting online orders measures use of the system, not whether the aim was met.
b.clue: Match the review to the indicator Hana set out to improve.

a.best: To compare the results and judge whether the change worked

b.best: Count complaints after a month and compare them with 40

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a precise detail: it repeats the figure of 40 from the stem, so a student could pick it by matching the number rather than by knowing the idea. Consider giving another option a specific figure too, such as comparing online orders with last month's sales.
